The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ have the standard product presentation, smooth structure, and period-one basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the upstream torus definition. Use its selected product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the right diagonal action and $BT=ET/T$. For a smooth left $T$-manifold $X$, define real Borel equivariant cohomology by $H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)=H^*(ET\times_T X;\mathbb R)$ using the quotient convention $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i$ is the class corresponding to the dual period-one basis vector $e_i^*$ and each $u_i$ has degree $2$.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. With the stated quotient convention, this is the Euler class of the Borel line $ET\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$, where $T$ acts on $\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$ by $\chi_m$. Use the complex-orientation convention $c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line $L$; thus $u_\chi$ is also the first Chern class of its Borel character line. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. Write $S^{-1}H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)$ and $S^{-1}\mathcal R$ for the fraction localizations: $a/s=a'/s'$ if $t(s'a-sa')=0$ for some $t\in S$, and $(a/s)+(b/t)=(ta+sb)/(st)$; the module structure is induced by the coefficient-ring localization. The coefficient-ring identification is used under AC: the upstream classifying-space cohomology proof invokes AC in its Künneth and coefficient arguments.

If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. Define its pushforward explicitly as follows. For $N\geq0$ put $B_N=(\mathbb{CP}^N)^r$, $X_N=(S^{2N+1})^r\times_T X$, and $p_N:X_N\to B_N$; the compatible finite Hopf bundles in the chosen Milnor model give $j_N:B_N\to BT$ and $a_N:X_N\to X_T$. Give $X_N$ the orientation of the complex-oriented base followed by that of $X$. For $a\in H^q(X_N;\mathbb R)$ define $(p_N)_!a$ by the perfect-duality equation $\langle b\smile(p_N)_!a,[B_N]\rangle=\langle p_N^*b\smile a,[X_N]\rangle$ for every complementary-degree $b$. For $\alpha\in H_T^q(X;\mathbb R)$ and $d=q-n\geq0$, choose $N$ with $2N+1\geq d$ and set $\int_X\alpha=(\pi_X)_!\alpha=(j_N^*)^{-1}(p_N)_!a_N^*\alpha$; set it to zero for $d<0$. Here $j_N^*$ is an isomorphism in degree $d$ because it is the polynomial quotient by $(u_1^{N+1},\ldots,u_r^{N+1})$, with each $u_i$ the restricted tautological Euler class, not a newly signed hyperplane class. The construction lemma proves existence and uniqueness of the finite pairing map, independence of $N$, base restriction compatibility, the projection formula, and compatibility with normalized right-Thom Gysin maps. In particular this map lowers degree by $n$, has values in $\mathcal R$, and its localized extension is $\int_X(\alpha/s)=(\int_X\alpha)/s$. For an oriented $T$-equivariant vector bundle $E\to X$ whose Borel-associated bundle has a normalized Thom class, define its equivariant Euler class $e_T(E)$ as the pullback of that Thom class by the zero section. The Thom class is normalized to restrict on each oriented fiber pair $(D^c,S^{c-1})$ to the positive generator of $H^c(D^c,S^{c-1};\mathbb R)$. For rank $c=0$, the Thom class and Euler class are $1$. For a complex representation line of character $\chi$, this convention gives Euler class $u_\chi$. For a fixed component $F$ of a $T$-action on $M$, the orientation convention is $o(TM|_F)=o(TF)\wedge o(\nu_F)$, where $\nu_F$ is its chosen equivariantly oriented normal bundle. This is the Borel convention; no identification with a Cartan, Chow, or quotient-stack cohomology model is assumed here.

Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ use the product Milnor model $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ with its ordinary product topology, and let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. $$ p:EG\longrightarrow BG $$

is a numerable principal $G$-bundle. The numeration satisfies the library's support-subordinate convention, not merely cozero containment.

$$e\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i,\qquad o\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i+1$$

are $G$-equivariantly homotopic to the identity. If $a,b:T\to EG$ are

Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a compact closed equivariant embedded boundaryless submanifold with invariant oriented normal bundle $\nu$ and $o(TX|_Y)=o(TY)\wedge o(\nu)$. Then

$u_\xi$ pulls back to $u_{f^*\xi}$.  A normalized Thom class is unique, and

with normalized Thom classes $u_E,u_F$ and Euler classes
$e(E),e(F)$. The coefficient ring $R$ is commutative and unital.

reversal assertion below applies only in positive rank. Both bases in a
pullback square are required to lie in the general Thom scope.

   $$
   \begin{CD} f^*E @>>> E\\ @VVV @VVV\\ B' @>f>> B\end{CD}
   $$
   one has $e(f^*E)=f^*e(E)$.
2. **Orientation sign.** Over $R=\mathbb Z$ and $m>0$, reversing the orientation of $E$
   negates the class: $e(E,-o)=-e(E,o)$.
3. **Whitney product.** Give $E\oplus F$ the ordered direct-sum orientation.
   Then $e(E\oplus F)=e(E)e(F)$, including the rank-zero unit $e(0_B)=1$.
4. **Koszul sign.** The swap $E\oplus F\to F\oplus E$ changes the ordered-sum

   standard orders satisfy
   $$e(E)e(F)=(-1)^{mn}e(F)e(E).$$

At $p\in F$, the exponential map of this invariant metric is $T$-equivariant and is injective on a sufficiently small ball in $T_pM$. Thus, for $v$ in that ball, $\exp_p(v)$ is fixed by every $t\in T$ exactly when $v$ is fixed by every linear map $d_pt$; the fixed set near $p$ is the exponential image of $(T_pM)^T$. Therefore $F$ is locally a smooth submanifold and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$. The fixed locus is closed in compact $M$, hence compact; its connected components are open in this locally connected manifold and compactness gives only finitely many.

The orthogonal complement of $(T_pM)^T$ in $T_pM$ is the normal fiber, so it contains no $T$-fixed vector. The complexification of an orthogonal representation of the abelian group $T$ is a commuting family of unitary maps and decomposes into simultaneous character eigenspaces; complex conjugation pairs the $\chi$ and $\bar\chi$ spaces. A real one-dimensional character would have image in $\{+1,-1\}$ and is trivial because $T$ is connected. Thus every nontrivial real summand is two-dimensional. Averaging the fiber action against a character gives a smooth idempotent projection on the complexified normal bundle. Its rank is locally constant and hence constant on connected $F_j$. At one point only finitely many characters occur, since the fiber has finite dimension; constant ranks therefore imply exactly those finitely many characters occur everywhere on $F_j$. The real conjugate-pair subbundles are consequently smooth.

all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

derivations.claim: The Hopf bundle has smooth local sections over the affine projective charts, obtained by choosing the distinguished unit coordinate positive real. Their transition functions are smooth circle-valued functions. Finite products give smooth principal $T$ charts for $E_N\to B_N$, and the associated charts $p_N^{-1}(U)\cong U\times X$ have smooth transition $(b,x)\mapsto(b,t(b)x)$. Thus $X_N$ is a smooth boundaryless manifold of dimension $b_N+n$. It is compact Hausdorff as the quotient of compact $E_N\times X$ by a compact-group action, and second countable by these finitely many base charts and a countable atlas of $X$. The transition maps preserve vertical orientation and hence the base-then-fiber total orientation. The same statements hold for $Y_N$, and its normal bundle is $E_N\times_T\nu$.

For $0\leq d=q-n\leq b_N$, the right side of the defining pairing is a linear functional on $H^{b_N-d}(B_N;k)$, so [F3] supplies a unique class in $H^d(B_N;k)$. If $d<0$, its putative test degree exceeds $b_N$; both the test group and the target are zero. If $d>b_N$, then $q>b_N+n$, the source is zero and so is the target. This defines the finite-stage map in all degrees, with no choice of a dual basis.

For real coefficients construct a second finite-stage map directly on forms. More generally let $p:E\to B$ be any smooth bundle with closed oriented compact $n$-dimensional fiber and orientation-preserving structure group. For $\omega\in\Omega^{n+d}(E)$, evaluate $I_p\omega$ on $d$ tangent vectors at $b$ by lifting them to $E|_b$, inserting the lifts first in $\omega$, and integrating the resulting vertical $n$-form over $E|_b$. Changing a lift by a vertical vector produces $n+1$ vertical insertions and hence zero, so this definition is independent of lifts. In a bundle chart with coordinates $b$ on the base and oriented fiber coordinates $y$, write base differentials before fiber differentials; $I_p$ integrates exactly the coefficients of $db^I\wedge dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n$. A finite fiber partition reduces to smooth coefficient functions supported in a fixed compact coordinate box. For each base derivative, the difference quotients converge uniformly on that box to the corresponding derivative, by the fundamental theorem of calculus and uniform continuity of the next derivative; integration therefore commutes with that derivative. Iteration proves the integrated coefficients are smooth. Fiber coordinate changes agree by oriented change of variables. Thus this is a global, explicitly defined form; it is zero for $d<0$.

In the local formula, horizontal differentiation passes under the integral. Terms from vertical differentiation integrate to zero by Stokes, since the fiber has no boundary; one may use a partition on the fiber and the derivatives of its sum cancel. Consequently $dI_p\omega=I_p d\omega$. Moreover $I_p(p^*\eta\wedge\omega)=\eta\wedge I_p\omega$. For a smooth base map $f:B'\to B$, the pullback bundle has precisely the same vertical integral evaluated on $df$ of the lifted vectors, proving $f^*I_p=I_{p'}\widetilde f^*$, with no transversality requirement on $f$. Fubini proves the iterated formula, ordering vertical coordinates as the first fiber followed by the second. All statements hold for vertically compactly supported forms on vector-bundle tubes as well.

We verify the trace identity at a finite stage. For positive normal rank, on the disk normal bundle $D
u_N$ of the compact embedded $Y_N\subset X_N$, represent its real relative Thom class by a closed form supported in the interior. Here is the relative comparison needed for this assertion. Integration on the two spaces of the pair $(D
u_N,S
u_N)$ commutes with restriction. The induced map on mapping cones is a quasi-isomorphism: the long exact sequences of the two cones and the absolute isomorphisms [F4] prove injectivity and surjectivity by the exact-sequence diagram chase. The singular cone computes relative cohomology. On the form side restriction to the boundary is surjective by a collar and cutoff, so the cone also computes the kernel of restriction. On a collar a closed representative restricting to zero on the boundary is exact, by integrating its normal-coordinate contraction; subtracting the derivative of a cutoff times this primitive makes it vanish on a smaller collar. It therefore extends by zero as a closed form $	au$ on the open normal tube. Its fiber integral is $1$: on each oriented disk fiber, extend the collar-vanishing form by zero to the oriented double sphere. Excision sends the positive disk-relative generator to the positive top class of that sphere. Naturality of the relative comparison identifies its de Rham image with this extension, and [F4] evaluates its sphere integral as $1$. Thus its disk integral is $1$, with the stated orientation, and Thom normalization supplies exactly this relative generator. Thus $I_{
u_N}	au=1$.

For a closed base form $\eta$ of complementary degree, Fubini gives $\int_B\eta\wedge I_p\omega=\int_Ep^*\eta\wedge\omega$. Apply [F4] and the perfect pairing [F3] to $p_N$ to see that the cohomology map of $I_{p_N}$ is exactly the map of step 2.1 under de Rham comparison. Hence the finite-stage singular map over $\mathbb R$ has the base-change and projection properties of step 3.1. This proves those properties of the actual pairing-defined map, not of an unrelated candidate.

Coefficient inclusion is injective on rational cohomology of any space here. Indeed, split cycles and boundaries in its free rational singular complex; [F3]'s field UCT gives $H^q(-;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H_q(-;\mathbb Q),\mathbb Q)$, and extension to $\mathbb R$ sends a functional to its scalar extension, which is injective. Extension is exact over a field, so homology also extends by scalars. On our compact manifolds the cohomology groups are finite dimensional by [F3]; their scalar-extended pairing is the real perfect pairing, since fundamental classes and cup evaluation commute with coefficients on chains. Uniqueness in step 2.1 therefore identifies the realification of the rational pushforward with the real pushforward. Real base-change and projection identities between rational classes now imply the rational identities by injectivity.

The square from $X_N\to X_{N+1}$ over $B_N\to B_{N+1}$ is a pullback square of smooth bundles: restriction of the larger Hopf bundle is the smaller one, and associated-bundle formation commutes with restriction. Steps 4.1 and 5.1 give $\iota_N^*(p_{N+1})_!a_{N+1}^*\alpha=(p_N)_!a_N^*\alpha$. By [F2] and change of coefficients, $H^*(B_N;k)=k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]/(u_1^{N+1},\ldots,u_r^{N+1})$, and $j_N^*$ is the polynomial quotient map from $H^*(BT;k)=k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$. Its first possible killed monomial has degree $2N+2$, so it is an isomorphism in degrees $d\leq2N+1$. Compatibility thus identifies all sufficiently large finite outputs with a single degree-$d$ polynomial. This proves existence, independence, and uniqueness in the Statement. Restriction from a larger stable index also proves the asserted equality at every smaller index. No cohomological limit theorem for $X_T$ is used.

Represent a real class $\beta_N$ by a closed form $\zeta$ on $Y_N$. The Gysin image is represented by extension by zero of $q^*\zeta\wedge\tau$, where $q$ is the tube projection. This follows from the relative comparison of step 3.2, relative multiplicativity and tubular excision. For clarity, the natural wedge/cup cochain homotopy of [[lem-de-rham-integration-respects-wedge-and-cup-in-cohomology]] also proves relative multiplicativity here: its restriction to the boundary vanishes when the Thom-form factor vanishes there, so its coboundary identity descends to the relative complexes. This is the relative product actually used, rather than an assumed multiplicative mapping-cone comparison. Integration over the normal fibers gives $\zeta$ by step 3.1 and $I_q\tau=1$. In total orientation the tangent directions of $Y_N$ precede the oriented normal directions, exactly as specified in the Statement; Fubini therefore gives $(p_N)_!i_{N*}\beta_N=(p_{Y,N})_!\beta_N$. Rational Thom classes map to normalized real Thom classes by [F6], so rational equality follows by step 5.1.

To check the projection formula for homogeneous $v\in H^*(BT;k)$, choose $N$ large enough that restriction detects both output degrees of $\int_X(\pi_X^*v\smile\alpha)$ and $v\smile\int_X\alpha$. The finite-stage projection formula makes their restrictions equal; injectivity in step 6.1 proves equality on $BT$. Finite sums give the formula for arbitrary classes. Coefficient compatibility follows in the same way. Restriction to $B_0=*$ is ordinary integration, by the defining perfect pairing in dimension zero and [F4]. For a trivial action the form integral on $B_N\times X$ gives the stated tensor formula and the product rule by Fubini; rational statements follow from step 5.1. The fraction formulas in [F6] now extend this module-linear map uniquely to the localization; an equality witnessed by $t(s'\alpha-s\alpha')=0$ remains an equality after applying the linear map.

Restrict the supplied Borel Thom class and tubular map to $B_N$. Thom naturality [F6] and naturality of relative cup product and excision identify this restriction of $i_*^T\beta$ with $i_{N*}\beta_N$. Apply step 6.2 and detect the resulting output class at a stable $N$ by step 6.1. This proves $\int_X i_*^T\beta=\int_Y\beta$ and its localized extension. Empty fibers give zero throughout; rank-zero normal bundles have standard Thom class $1$: their Thom map is the identity on $Y_T$, and tubular extension to $X_T$ is extension by zero from the open-and-closed union of components $Y_T$. For $r=0$ every base is a point, so the same construction is ordinary oriented integration with no limiting step. Negative output degrees are zero at every finite stage. These observations complete the construction in all the stated cases.
